newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise further as Brazil fears ease.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise further as Brazil fears ease.

text.p: Argentine bonds advanced further in early trade Thursday, putting fears about Brazilian real devaluation behind them but with modest trading volume, dealers said.
"The market is strong and everything indicates an upwards trajectory," said bond analyst Juan Carlos Bermudez. "Worries about a Brazilian currency devaluation have been overcome."

The market had fallen sharply Tuesday on worries about the Real, but rebounded Wednesday with the help of good U.S. indicators and the sale of the 10 percent employees' stake in Argentine oil giant YPF, which continued to boost bonds Thursday.
"The YPF share placing at $29.25 each was positive for the market, which looks like returning to its firm outlook for the medium term," said one dealer.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was up 1/5 at 94.50 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was little changed at 118.25.
